Across the Cosmos Podcast: Episode 43 - Political Correctness and Free Speech (part 1)

In the novel 1984 by George Orwell, a bleak portrait of a dystopian future is painted whereupon most of earth’s inhabitants are relegated to little more than the status of cattle. This more than eighty percent of the total population, the Proletariat, are a people kept intentionally ignorant so as to be of service to the Upper Class, a group of people which comprise only two percent of the total population.

Part of the strategy to keep this lowest of the classes ignorant is to stunt their speech. By removing the ability to adequately articulate their grievances, the Upper Class removes the threat of rebellion. The logic being that one cannot mount an offensive against that which one cannot describe.

George Orwell (real name Eric Blair) did not conceptualize this tactic on his own; it was already a well used tactic, most recently employed by the Nazis and the Soviet Union. It would later be used in China and in Cambodia. The death toll would steadily mount in each of those countries as the Upper Class took greater and greater control of the ignorant populous.

Many readying this opening and listening to this week’s podcast may believe that I am once again engaging in hyperbole, but sadly that is not the case. The United States today is under siege. We are a people who are terrified of being labeled racist, homophobic, chauvinistic, Islamophobic, etc. We are a people who are willingly leaving behind our principles and convictions for the off-chance that we will find favor with those who seek to find offense. This is a fantasy.

Those who seek to find offense do so primarily to seek power and control over others. There will be no détente between those who seek offenses and those who capitulate; there will only be the conqueror and the conquered.

Join Chase Rockwell, Lou Rodgers and Dave Cameron as they discuss this modern-day Trojan Horse: Political Correctness and the trampling of our rights to Free Speech.

Find us here at: http://www.acrossthecosmos.com

This was back before they new how big this field was, and were just beginning to suspect how enormous the Ghawar Field could possibly be. Oil was discovered in the field in the very late 1940s. Interesting Anecdote - Britain was given first shot at producing and selling oil discovered in Saudi Arabia. Sir Lancelot Oliphant, told the Saudis in the 1930s they were nuts to expect the British Empire to pay for the drilling and exploration costs to find and sell any oil discovered. He thought they had no oil and just wanted British to lease miles of useless land. Luckily for the USA some Texans were happy to make a deal with Saudi Arabia - leading to the greatest oil find in history, creating the famous"petrodollar," starting the Saudi-USA strategic alliance, and hugely enriching the USA and Saudi Arabia. Not to mention changing the 20th century. It could have been Britain and the "petropound" world reserve currency. The original Saudi oil company was known until 1988 as the "Arabian-American Oil Company." The U.S. companies that did most Saudi exploration in the beginning were Texaco and SoCal (California Standard Oil - after T. Roosevelt broke the huge standard oil trust monopoly). Most of Texaco was also once Standard Oil. To give an idea how rich the Rockefellers are - almost the entire Getty oil fortune came from a very small sized drilling concession in Saudi Arabia which Getty paid Ibn Saud $9.5 million for the rights to its oil for 60 years. It looked like a barren wasteland.. However that little piece of land produced 16,000,000 barrels of oil a year for Getty and was the source of most of his fortune.
